I have farmed these 12.4 mu in Quzhou County for 30 years, and I know what works on this land. My household has six people, and some of my children work off-farm in the city, so I must be careful with labor—especially during the busy wheat harvest and maize sowing window in early June. I have well water, which is reliable but costs electricity, so I irrigate at the critical stages and not more.

My 10 mu follow the wheat–maize double-cropping system that every household around here uses. The wheat was sown last October and is now waking up in early spring; the maize will go into the same field right after the wheat is cut in June. I keep 2.4 mu for stevia because the buyers pay about 6 yuan per jin for the dried leaves, and that cash helps pay for school fees and fertilizer.

For the **wheat** on 10 mu, I use an improved local variety such as Shi Mai or Lumai—the seed is cheap and trustworthy. I will irrigate four times: now at green-up, again at jointing, once at heading, and a final time during grain filling. I do rotary tillage before sowing (done last autumn). For fertilizer, I spread compound fertilizer as a basal dose and topdress with urea at green-up and jointing; in total that comes to about 16 kg of nitrogen, 7 kg of phosphorus, and 4 kg of potassium per mu. I spray herbicide once and add insecticide and fungicide when I see problems—about four sprays in all. I expect roughly 950 kg per mu if the weather holds.

For **summer maize** on the same 10 mu, there is no time to plough after wheat harvest. I plant hybrid seed—Nongda 372 or Denghai 605—directly with no-tillage. These hybrids yield well and resist lodging. I put down compound fertilizer at sowing and perhaps a little extra nitrogen at the big-flare stage, totaling about 18 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once when the plants are knee-high and again at flowering. Three pesticide applications are enough. I expect about 1,100 kg per mu.

For **stevia** on 2.4 mu, I plant improved cuttings—about 8,000 plants per mu—in mid-April. Stevia leaves are money, so I apply both compound fertilizer and some organic manure, and I irrigate five times to keep the crop lush. Insects and mildew love stevia, so I spray more often than for grain—about 10 times with insecticide and fungicide. I do rotary tillage before planting. Harvest will be in late August or early September, and I expect about 500 kg of dry leaves per mu.
